# Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga (Vb 15)

**ID:** Vb 15
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/vb15
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh02m.mul14.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga* is the fifteenth chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994; SuttaCentral]. In the Pali Text Society edition, it occupies pages 293–305 [Jayatilleke 1963]. Like other major treatises of the *Vibhaṅga*, it provides systematic analysis through divisions such as the Sutta explanation (*suttantabhājaniya*) [Hazra 1994; Nyanatiloka 1938]. The treatise is structured around the four analytical discriminations (*catu-paṭisambhidā*, corresponding to Buddhist Sanskrit *pratisaṃvidā*): the discrimination of meaning (*attha-paṭisambhidā*), the discrimination of phenomena, causal conditions, or doctrine (*dhamma-paṭisambhidā*), the discrimination of language or verbal definition (*nirutti-paṭisambhidā*), and the discrimination of perspicuity or analytical insight (*paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā*) [Jayatilleke 1963; Nyanatiloka 1938; Peoples 2013]. The text articulates these principles as systematic criteria for developing analytical knowledge, distinguishing between mundane and supramundane realizations [Peoples 2013].

In comparative literature, SuttaCentral identifies a parallel in the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścaya-sūtra* (§ 24, *Catasraḥ Pratisaṁvidaḥ*) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates massive Pali-internal text reuse (over 8,000 matches), most prominently with fellow *Vibhaṅga* sections (such as the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* and *Sikkhāpadavibhaṅga*) and various books of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (including *Abyākatavipāka*, *Lokuttaravipāka*, and *Ahetukakiriyāabyākata*) [DharmaNexus]. Close doctrinal and phraseological parallels are also shared with the *Ñāṇakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, as well as its commentary and the *Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā* (*Sammohavinodanī*) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with Sanskrit and Tibetan treatises treating the discriminations and Abhidharma categories, including Vimalamitra's *Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti*, Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, the Tibetan *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā*, and Chinese Āgama collections (*Ekottarika Āgama* and *Dīrgha Āgama*) [DharmaNexus].
